name: Aegis Personal Systems WardCloak WC-2 'Ghost'
description:
A lightweight jacket with integrated micro-emitters in the lining that, when activated, projects a localized visual distortion field around the wearer. The WC-2 does not render the user invisible — instead, it creates a visual 'smear' effect that makes the wearer's outline indistinct and difficult to track, similar to looking at a figure through heavily textured glass. The distortion is most effective in low-light conditions and against optical systems that rely on edge detection algorithms.

Aegis developed the WC-2 after market research showed that many self-defense encounters could be avoided entirely if the potential victim was simply harder to see. The jacket's distortion field runs on a distributed battery network woven into the garment's lining, providing twelve minutes of continuous distortion on a full charge. The activation switch is inside the left pocket, accessible without removing the hand. The jacket itself is a nondescript urban design available in charcoal, navy, and dark green.

The WC-2 is priced at Φ1,600, positioning it as a premium tier investment. Its primary market is people who commute through high-risk areas during low-light hours — night-shift workers, late-service employees, anyone who regularly walks through places where being visible makes you a target. The distortion effect has limitations: it is ineffective in bright light, does not defeat thermal imaging, and the micro-emitter grid creates a faint shimmer visible to anyone who knows what to look for.
specifications:
distortion type: visual edge disruption
effective conditions: low-light, artificial lighting
duration: 12 minutes continuous
charging: removable battery pack, 3-hour charge
jacket weight: 680 g (including electronics)
available sizes: XS-3XL
available colors: charcoal, navy, dark green
cost: Φ1,600
limitations: ineffective in daylight, does not defeat thermal imaging
tactical_use: Activate before entering high-risk areas rather than in response to a threat — the distortion needs to be active before the attacker selects you as a target. Move steadily through low-light areas; the distortion is most effective when the wearer is in motion, as stationary silhouettes are easier to resolve through the interference. The WC-2 is a prevention tool, not a combat tool — if an attacker has already engaged, the distortion provides minimal advantage.
cultural_context: The WC-2 has introduced a new concept to GLMZ's personal defense market: avoidance as defense. Rather than tools that react to attacks, it prevents targeting entirely. This philosophy has resonated with residents who are tired of the escalation cycle where better defense tools lead to more aggressive attackers. Some urban safety advocates call the WC-2 the most ethical defense product on the market because it prevents conflict rather than winning it. Critics note that only people who can afford Φ1,600 get to be invisible.
story_hooks: Security forces have complained that WC-2 wearers are invisible to their patrol algorithms, creating blind spots in surveillance coverage that criminals have begun to exploit — not by committing crimes in the jackets, but by mapping the blind spots the jackets create.

Aegis has received reports that a competitor has reverse-engineered the micro-emitter grid and is selling distortion panels that can be sewn into any garment — destroying Aegis's monopoly on wearable visual distortion.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, contemporary urban bomber or harrington jacket with an almost imperceptible shimmer across the lining when powered. At rest, it appears as an ordinary commuter garment — understated and forgettable. When active, a faint iridescent ripple plays across the wearer's silhouette, like heat distortion or a troubled window reflection.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 62–75 cm (depending on size); Sleeve length: 58–70 cm; Chest width (laid flat): 48–58 cm; Collar to hem: standard jacket proportions
physical_description.weight_description: Noticeably heavier than a standard jacket due to the embedded battery network and micro-emitter grid, but well-balanced and distributed — feels substantial without being burdensome, approximately 680g total
physical_description.primary_material: Water-resistant synthetic polymer outer shell with elasticated trimming; the inner lining contains a gossamer-thin photonic interference grid woven into microfiber batting
physical_description.finish: Matte textile exterior with subtle articulated stitching; inner lining has a soft silken texture that conceals the crystalline micro-emitter nodes. Battery pack (removable from rear inner pocket) is brushed gunmetal with soft-touch rubber accents
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal, navy, or dark green outer shell; silver-white photonic grid visible only when active or under close inspection; battery pack in dark gray
physical_description.grip_texture: Outer fabric is smooth, slightly textured polyester; inner pockets lined with soft microsuede; the activation switch inside the left pocket is smooth polymer, slightly recessed
distinctive_features: Barely-visible micro-emitter nodes arranged in a grid pattern along the inner lining — only noticeable under close inspection or direct light
Faint shimmer or iridescent ripple visible across the wearer's outline when the distortion field is active
Removable battery pack with LED charge indicator (green/amber/red) housed in a rear interior compartment
Minimalist branding: small woven Aegis Personal Systems label on inner collar, no obvious tactical design cues
Articulated seams and ventilation apertures positioned for unrestricted movement
Hidden activation switch recessed into left interior pocket — deliberately unobtrusive
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Aegis Personal Systems woven label on inner collar (upper right); small embossed serial plate inside rear battery compartment; model designation WC-2 printed on the interior tag alongside size and care instructions
physical_description.condition_typical: When new: pristine, with faint warehouse handling marks. In regular field use: minimal wear on outer shell, battery pack shows minor scuff marks from repeated removals, seams remain tight, lining undamaged. After prolonged use: possible fading on outer fabric, slight wear at pocket edges, battery contacts show light oxidation
